lessons.content:
PAGE_1:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 1 Next Level Website Content – Checklist   Introduction ü Website content needs to attract prospects and further your business goals ü Simply updating your blog isn’t enough ü Effective web content needs to: o Increase awareness of your brand o Engage your target o Forge a connection with your audience o Generate and convert more quality leads o Boost search engine ranking  ü You might find that after the initial rush of a website launch, visits start to fall ü If this is the case, your web content, and the way your website is structured, could be the culprit.   ü Developing a business website isn't a one-time event. It’s an ongoing process ü Apply web content and keyword strategies to take a big leap forward

PAGE_2:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 2 The Evolution of Web Content ü Your website should attract and appeal to people who are looking for what you’re selling ü It’s critical to understand who your audience is and how they find you ü Search engines act as a matchmaker between you and your audience ü Search engines have changed over the years, and your content must adapt along with it ü In the past, people increased search engine page rank simply by adding keywords and backlinks ü This strategy no longer gets you optimal results ü Search engines changed their algorithms to rank sites more efficiently based on value for the reader ü This means that small businesses need to adapt  Here is your roadmap through the course:           Laying the FoundationRethink Your Website Design and StructureIncorporate Long-Form Content into Your WebsiteThree Long-Form Content Strategies to Boost Site RankingAdd Short-Form Content to the MixCapture Audience Attention with a Content Series

PAGE_3:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 3 Learning Objectives:  ü Evaluate and analyze your target audience and conduct a website content review. ü Identify where you need to update the structure of your website and how essential pages are presented. ü Recognize the importance of long-form content and pick tangible ways to incorporate it into your site. ü Apply long-form content strategies (Pillar, Skyscraper, and Ladder) to increase site visits and boost search engine ranking. ü Use online tools and audience feedback to generate new content ideas. ü Identify ways to incorporate different content series (Welcome, Buzz-Building) into your overall web content strategy. ü Consolidate and implement your learning and plan future action steps    Expectations Before we start the course, take a minute to think about what you want to get out of it. In the Action Guide, write down three skills you expect to gain.

PAGE_4:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 4 Module 1 – Laying the Foundation: Evaluate Your Target Audience & Content  Learning Objective:  ü Evaluate and analyze your target audience and conduct a website content review.   ü Take stock of where your site currently stands ü The two most important elements to review are: o Your target audience o Your existing content ü Your content needs to resonate with your audience  Understand Your Target Audience  ü It is always a good idea to periodically reexamine current followers, customers, and potential customers  ü If there has been a shift, you will need to adapt your content to appeal to your evolving audience ü Focus on the following areas: o Demographics o Psychographics o Purchasing Behavior

PAGE_5:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 5 Demographics ü These include unemotional, fact-based information about your audience: o Age o Geographic location o Education level o Marital status o Occupation  Psychographics ü Psychographics explore the emotional and personal information about your audience, including:  o Needs and desires o Values o Hobbies o Goals o Pain points (areas where they're struggling)  Purchasing Behavior ü Ask yourself questions about your market and how they interact with your product or service ü Here are some ways to learn more: o Observe how they interact with your product, service or relevant topics o Follow their activity on relevant forums o Keep track of social media posts (yours and the competition's) that generate the most interest and interaction o Speak with your audience directly

PAGE_6:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 6 ü You’ll use this information to create content that appeals to your audience overall ü Focus on characteristics that your audience shares  ü Understand your audience and don’t be afraid to ask them what they want  Conduct a Website Content Review ü Create a list of pages on your site  How to Locate All of Your Website Pages ü Manually creating a list is inefficient and time-consuming ü Here are a few options to help generate a complete list quickly: o Online sitemap generator o WordPress plug-in o Google Analytics  Content Evaluation – Step by Step ü Follow this process to determine wat stays, what goes, and what needs to be improved or expanded: o Identify essential pages o Check the competition o Keep your target in mind o Evaluate each page ü Questions to ask yourself when evaluating website content: o How fresh is this content?  o Is this content irrelevant or out of date? Does it reflect poorly on my brand? Does it undermine my reputation?

PAGE_7:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 7 o Does this content feature incorrect or expired pricing, discounts, offers, events? o Is the 'fine print' content up to date? (Policies, rules, ingredient list, mailing information etc.) o Are your search engine keywords represented prominently, yet naturally?

PAGE_8:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 8  Action Steps: 1. Before you take your web content to the next level, it’s helpful to understand who your audience is and what kind of content they want. Reflect and write down answers to these questions: Ø Who is your target audience? Focus on demographics, psychographics, and online behavior Ø What are some of the problems or issues your customer base has expressed?  Ø What subjects are they passionate about? What causes or organizations do they identify with?  2. Analyze what has worked for you in the past and apply these learnings to future content. Review your social media and blog posts and pages with the most interactions or visits, and ask yourself: Ø What do these pages and posts have in common? Ø What questions did the content answer?  Ø What comments stand out?   3. It will be easier to work with your sitemap if it's in a spreadsheet. To do this, convert the XML file you created into a CSV file using an online converter like onlinexmltools. Once the data is saved as a CSV file, it can easily be imported into Excel or other spreadsheet software. 4. Conduct your website review using your sitemap spreadsheet.  Highlight what to keep, redirect, or change/expand based on the step-by-step process in the module: Ø Identify essential pages Ø Check the competition  Ø Keep your target in mind  Ø Evaluate each page Use different colors for each to help with sorting and prioritizing which pages you want to work on first.

PAGE_9:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 9 Module 2 – Rethink Your Website Design and Structure  Learning Objective:  ü Identify where you need to update the structure of your website and how essential pages are presented.  ü How you structure and present information can affect whether people decide to stay on your site ü Make sure you have these four key pages on your site: o Start Here o Home o About Us o Blog  ü Customize how information is presented based on your target audience, values, mission, and your unique offering. ü Consider streamlining your home page/welcome portal if you have two distinct audiences ü This prevents cluttering and unnecessary information ü Be open to challenging convention   The Upside-Down Home Page ü The Upside-Down Home Page reprioritizes the order of your home page ü The idea is to put the most important information up top ü The rest of the information follows, and navigation is moved to the bottom

PAGE_10:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 10 Reinvent the About Page ü The About Page introduces visitors to you and your business, not your offering or content ü The content within the about page can be shaken up a bit  Find New Ways to Introduce Yourself ü A personal welcome video  ü Explainer video about your company ü A 'before/after' photo that illustrates your evolution ü Your answers to a questionnaire ü A guided tour ü Choose something appropriate to your industry and personality ü Your About Page should always further the primary goal of your website ü Every about page is different, depending on your audience and what will resonate   Add a Manifesto Page ü Add a manifesto only if it’s relevant to your brand and you have a good ‘why’ story  Add an Internal Search Tool on Your Website ü Don’t forget your internal search capabilities as you grow your site content ü Benefits of an internal search tool include: o Keeps visitors on your site o Allows you to gain insight into your visitors o Inspires new content and keyword ideas

PAGE_11:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 11 ü Add internal search tools to your site ü Website structure and design has to be constantly re-evaluated and improved   Action Steps: 1. Go to your Home page and answer these questions: Ø Currently, what is the dominant piece of information or image? Does it further your business goals?  Ø When people land on your Home page, is it immediately apparent what you are selling or what services you offer? Ø Brainstorm ways that you can improve your Home page. 2. Reflect on your personal story and your brand's story and answer these questions: Ø What sets you apart from the competition? Have you included this on your About page?  Ø Is there another way to tell your story that would be more appealing to your target audience?
